record.original_question: Fix n ≥ 1 and finite posets P, Q_0, ..., Q_m such that each Q_i extends P. Is there an algorithm that, given these finite posets, determines whether every embedding f: P → D_n can be extended to an embedding g: Q_i → D_n for some index i ≤ m, where the successful index i is allowed to depend on the chosen embedding of P into D_n?

evidence.quote: (b) The recognition problem for the possibility of embedding extensions. We clarify whether there exists an algorithm which, given finite posets P → Q0,...,Qn, n ≥ 0, allows us to determine whether any embedding f : P → Dn can be extended to an embedding g : Qi → Dn for some i ≤ n. (Clearly, here i depends on the choice of an embedding of P in Dn.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and let D_n denote the partial order of n-computably enumerable Turing degrees (so D_1 is the partial order of c.e. Turing degrees, D_2 is the partial order of d.c.e. degrees, and in general D_n is the partial order of n-c.e. degrees). For finite partially ordered sets P and Q, write P ↪ Q to indicate that P is a subposet of Q (i.e., Q extends P). 

Question: Does there exist an algorithm with the following input/output behavior?

• Input: a finite poset P, a positive integer m, and finite posets Q_0, Q_1, …, Q_m, each extending P (i.e., P ↪ Q_i for every i ≤ m).

• Output: "yes" if every order-preserving embedding f : P → D_n can be extended to an order-preserving embedding g : Q_i → D_n for some index i ≤ m (where the index i may depend on the embedding f), and "no" otherwise.

Determine whether such a decision procedure exists for each fixed n ≥ 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The recognition problem for the possibility of embedding extensions into the n-c.e. degrees is listed as an open problem in the 2015 survey on the structural theory of degrees of unsolvability. Related decidability results are known for the existential and ∀∃-theories of c.e. degrees in restricted forms, but no algorithm answering this exact extension-of-embeddings recognition question is reported in the literature found via search; the problem appears to remain open.
